# Types of Men to Avoid

Everyone has a personal "type" when it comes to attraction. Some people are drawn to tall, dark, and handsome partners, while others prefer a quieter, more intellectual companion. Whatever your particular preference may be, there are certain types of men that should be avoided by everyone, regardless of individual taste. Here are a few of the worst offenders to watch out for.

## The OverSharer

The OverSharer has no concept of privacy when it comes to your relationship. He broadcasts intimate details to his family, posts them for his blog readers, and will happily recount your most personal moments to anyone else who will listen. Nothing is off-limits, and no boundary is respected. What should remain between the two of you quickly becomes public knowledge, leaving you feeling exposed and betrayed.

## The OverThinker

The OverThinker turns even the most innocuous comment into an exhausting ordeal. He wastes hours dissecting a simple remark, analyzing it for hidden tone and secret meaning that was never there in the first place. A casual "I'm tired tonight" can spiral into an interrogation about whether you're losing interest. This constant overanalysis creates unnecessary tension and drains the energy out of an otherwise healthy relationship.

## The OverTalker

The OverTalker dominates every conversation. He interrupts, talks over you, and steamrolls through discussions until you can barely get a word in edgewise. Your thoughts and opinions are drowned out beneath his endless monologue, and over time you may find yourself giving up on speaking altogether. A relationship should be a dialogue, not a one-man show.

## The OverDresser

Finally, there's the OverDresser—an excessively fussy dandy who takes longer than you to get ready. He obsessively coordinates his outfits, frets over every accessory, and can't leave the house until every detail is perfect. While taking pride in one's appearance is admirable, this level of vanity can be exhausting and self-absorbed, leaving little room for anyone or anything else.

---

While attraction is deeply personal, these particular types share one common trait: they make relationships harder than they need to be. Recognizing the warning signs early can save you a great deal of frustration down the road.

# Nine Men You Should Definitely Not Date (Trust Me, I've Done the Research)

Let me start with a confession: I have terrible taste in men. Not "he forgot my birthday" terrible—more like "he brought his ex-girlfriend to our third date to get her opinion on me" terrible. After years of what I now generously call "field research," I've compiled a definitive list of nine problematic types of men that all women should avoid. Consider this your survival guide, written in the blood, sweat, and awkward brunch conversations of someone who learned these lessons the hard way.

Today, I'm covering the first four categories—the ones I like to call "The Overs." Because if there's one thing these men have in common, it's a spectacular inability to do anything in moderation.

## 1. The OverSharer

We've all met him. The OverSharer is the man who, within the first fifteen minutes of meeting you, will explain in vivid detail why his therapist thinks his mother is responsible for his commitment issues.

I once went on a coffee date with an OverSharer who, before our lattes even arrived, had told me about his colonoscopy results, his credit score, and the exact moment he lost his virginity (a story that involved a trampoline and, inexplicably, his cousin's bar mitzvah). By the time I finished my drink, I knew more about this man than I know about most members of my own family.

Here's the thing: emotional vulnerability is wonderful. But there's a difference between being open and treating your date like a confessional booth with legs. If he's crying about his childhood pet before you've learned his last name, run.

## 2. The OverThinker

The OverThinker cannot make a decision to save his life. Where would you like to eat? He doesn't know. He's been analyzing the menu of every restaurant within a ten-mile radius for the past two hours and has now entered a state of complete paralysis.

I dated an OverThinker who once texted me seventeen times debating whether his previous text had been "too enthusiastic." He analyzed our relationship the way a conspiracy theorist analyzes grainy photographs—finding hidden meaning in everything, spiraling into elaborate theories, and ultimately convincing himself the world was against him.

The OverThinker will read a novel's worth of subtext into your simple "sounds good." He'll lie awake wondering if that period at the end of your sentence meant you were angry. Dating him is exhausting, mostly because you'll spend the entire relationship reassuring him that yes, you did mean it when you said you had a nice time.

## 3. The OverTalker

Ah, the OverTalker. Have you ever tried to have a conversation with a hurricane? That's dating the OverTalker.

This man does not converse—he broadcasts. I once sat through an entire dinner with an OverTalker who spoke for so long, so continuously, that I genuinely began to wonder if he was breathing through his ears. I attempted to share an anecdote about my job. He interrupted with a forty-minute monologue about his fantasy football league, his opinions on cryptocurrency, and a play-by-play recap of a podcast he'd listened to that morning.

By dessert, he still hadn't asked me a single question. I could have told him my name was Gerald and I was wanted in three states, and he wouldn't have noticed. The OverTalker doesn't want a partner; he wants an audience. And honey, you deserve better than a permanent front-row seat to the one-man show of his life.

## 4. The OverDresser

Now, I appreciate a well-groomed man as much as the next woman. But the OverDresser takes it to a level that borders on performance art.

The OverDresser owns more skincare products than a dermatologist's office and takes longer to get ready than you do. I once dated a man who refused to sit on my couch because he was worried about "compromising the structural integrity" of his blazer. On another occasion, he canceled our plans because it was drizzling and he didn't want to risk his suede loafers.

There's confidence, and then there's a man who loves his own reflection more than he could ever love you. When he spends more time in front of the mirror than he does looking at you, you already know how this story ends. You'll always be competing with the one true love of his life—himself—and I promise you, you will never win.

---

So there you have it: the first four horsemen of the dating apocalypse. Stay tuned for part two, where I'll introduce you to the remaining five—including the notorious "Mama's Boy" and the enigmatic "Ghost Who Somehow Keeps Coming Back."

Until then, keep your standards high and your exits clearly marked.

# The Frisky: A Place Where Everybody Belongs

There's something wonderfully inviting about a space that welcomes everybody with open arms. Whether you're looking for lighthearted entertainment, honest conversation, or a community that never takes itself too seriously, the right platform can make all the difference.

**The** heart of any great community is inclusivity. When a space is built for everybody, it doesn't matter where you come from, what you believe, or how you spend your days—there's always room for one more voice at the table.

## Why "Frisky" Matters

Life gets serious enough on its own, which is why a little **frisky** energy goes a long way. Being frisky isn't about being reckless; it's about embracing playfulness, curiosity, and a willingness to have fun. It's the spark that turns an ordinary afternoon into something memorable, the wink that says, "Let's not overthink this—let's enjoy it."

A frisky attitude keeps things fresh. It encourages people to laugh at themselves, try new things, and approach the world with a sense of adventure rather than dread.

## Bringing Everybody Together

The magic happens when playfulness meets community. **Everybody** has a story, a joke to share, or a quirky opinion worth hearing. When you create a space that celebrates individuality while keeping the mood light, you build something that people genuinely want to be part of.

So here's to the platforms, the communities, and the moments that remind us to stay a little frisky—because when everybody feels welcome, the fun is contagious.

---

*Whether you're here to unwind, connect, or simply smile, remember: the best experiences are the ones we share together.*

# 9 Types of Men Women Should Avoid (All of Whom Start With "Over-")

Let me set the scene: I have a "type." Everyone tells me this. My friends can spot him across a crowded bar like a hawk sighting a particularly emotionally unavailable field mouse. And after roughly one thousand years of dating (give or take a millennium), I've discovered that my "type" is actually nine distinct types of men, and every single one of them is prefixed with the word "over." It's uncanny. It's like my subconscious went to the prefix aisle and bought in bulk.

So learn from my mistakes, ladies. Here are the nine "Over" men to avoid at all costs.

## 1. The OverSharer

You've known him for eleven minutes and you already know about his childhood bedwetting, his mother's second divorce, and the exact texture of his last breakup. He treats first dates like a deposition. There is no small talk—only large, unsolicited talk. By dessert, you know his credit score AND his therapist's first name. Run.

## 2. The OverThinker

He read one message from you and has now constructed seventeen alternate realities based on your use of a period instead of an exclamation point. This is the guy who takes four business days to respond to "hey" because he's workshopping it. Dating a Ross Geller type sounds fun until you realize you're on a break you didn't agree to.

## 3. The OverSharer's Cousin: The OverExplainer

Ask him a simple question and prepare for a TED Talk. "Do you want Italian or Thai?" becomes a forty-five-minute lecture on the geopolitics of pasta. He mansplains things you literally told him about yourself. He once explained my own job to me. I *have* the job.

## 4. The OverPromiser

He's going to take you to Paris. He's going to introduce you to his family. He's going to change lightbulbs, fix your car, AND launch a startup—all by Thursday. He's basically a Michael Scott "declaring bankruptcy" energy, except with your entire relationship. Spoiler: the Paris trip becomes a Groupon to Olive Garden.

## 5. The OverAchiever

Nothing you do is impressive enough because he's simultaneously running a marathon, learning Mandarin, and disrupting an industry no one asked to be disrupted. Dating him feels like a performance review. You'll mention you cooked dinner and he'll casually note that he built the stove.

## 6. The OverGrooming Guy

He takes longer to get ready than you do, and his skincare routine has more steps than a NASA launch sequence. Which would be fine—self-care, king!—except he judges you for owning one (1) moisturizer. His bathroom looks like a Sephora exploded. You will never get mirror time again.

## 7. The OverProtective One

Sweet at first. Terrifying by month three. He needs to know where you are, who you're with, and why you laughed at that text. This is Joe Goldberg from *You* cosplaying as a boyfriend. Charming voice-over, deeply concerning behavior. If a man says "I just worry about you" more than a Victorian mother, exit stage left.

## 8. The OverConfident Legend

He has never once considered that he might be wrong about anything, ever. He orders for you (incorrectly), gives directions (also incorrectly), and describes himself as "basically a genius" with zero supporting evidence. Think Gaston, but with a LinkedIn premium account. He'll wink at himself in the mirror and you'll wonder where your twenties went.

## 9. The OverIt Guy

The final boss. He's emotionally checked out before you've even started. Everything is "whatever," "sure," or a single thumbs-up emoji that somehow contains a lifetime of apathy. Dating him is like trying to have a relationship with a screensaver. He's not playing hard to get—he's genuinely just not there.

---

**The takeaway?** If a man comes with a prefix, proceed with caution. And if you find one who's just, you know, *normal*—no modifiers, no red flags, no unsolicited TED Talks—marry him immediately. Or at least text him back within four business days.

# The Nine "Over" Boyfriends You Need to Break Up With Immediately

*A field guide to the men who take everything too far—and take up too much of your precious time*

Listen up, buttercups. I've been in the dating trenches longer than most reality TV franchises have been on the air, and I've collected more red flags than a Communist parade. After years of "research" (read: emotional damage), I've identified the nine deadly archetypes lurking in your DMs. Grab your wine and take notes.

---

## 1. The Overachiever

He color-codes his gym schedule and treats brunch like a business meeting. This man has a five-year plan, a ten-year plan, and a plan for what to do if the other plans fail. Dating an Overachiever is like being romantically involved with a LinkedIn notification. He'll ask about your "goals" on the first date like he's Ryan Gosling in *The Big Short* pitching you a subprime mortgage. Sweetie, I just wanted tacos.

## 2. The Oversharer

By minute four, you know about his childhood bedwetting, his mother's affair, and his diagnosed conditions—alphabetized. He treats a first date like a confessional booth and *you* are the priest, therapist, and mildly horrified stranger all at once. Think Ross Geller narrating every feeling he's ever had, forever. Run.

## 3. The Overthinker

He texts "hey" and then spends the next six hours analyzing whether the lowercase "h" made him seem too casual. This is the man who will construct an entire relationship arc in his mind and break up with the imaginary version of you before dessert arrives. He's basically Woody Allen without the movies to show for the neuroses.

## 4. The Overcompensator

The lifted truck. The gold chains. The way he mentions his "boat" (a kayak). This king of the peacock strut is louder than a Kardashian wedding and twice as staged. He's overcompensating for something, and honey, we all know what it is. Every conversation is a highlight reel he's directing, producing, and starring in.

## 5. The Overgrown Child

Thirty-four years old and his diet consists of cereal and unearned confidence. His apartment features a gaming chair worth more than his mattress and exactly zero plants that are alive. He's Peter Pan if Peter Pan owed you rent money. You wanted a partner; you got a fourth roommate who happens to kiss you.

## 6. The Overprotective

Sweet at first! Then you realize he's tracking your location "for safety" and interrogating your barista like he's the Winter Soldier. He'll frame his jealousy as *devotion*, which is exactly what Joe from *You* does right before—well, you've seen it. Love shouldn't come with a GPS ankle monitor, darling.

## 7. The Overpromiser

"We'll go to Paris!" "I'll fix your sink!" "I'm going to change!" This man makes commitments the way politicians make campaign promises—enthusiastically and never fulfilled. He has the follow-through of a broken Fitbit. He's charming as Don Draper pitching Kodak, but at the end of the pitch, you're still standing there with a leaky faucet and a dream.

## 8. The Overexplainer

Ask this man a yes-or-no question and prepare for a TED Talk. He'll mansplain the plot of a movie *you recommended to him.* He corrects your grammar mid-argument and once "well, actually'd" you about your own birthday. It's like dating the guy at the party who won't stop talking about crypto, except the party never, ever ends.

## 9. The Overhaul

The most dangerous of all. He's a *project.* You think, "With a little love, he'll blossom!" No, babe. You are not a HGTV renovation show, and he is not a fixer-upper with good bones. You'll pour in years of emotional labor and end up with a man who *finally* learned to text back the same week he starts dating someone new. You built the man; she gets the house.

---

**The takeaway, my loves:** You deserve a boyfriend whose only "Over" is that he's absolutely *over the moon* about you. Anything less, and it's time to swipe left on the whole situation.

Now go pour yourself another glass. You've earned it. 💅

# The Definitive Guide to Men You Should Absolutely Never Date (A Survival Manual)

*Because your therapist deserves a vacation too*

Ladies, we've all been there. You match with someone who seems normal, only to discover three dates in that he refers to his mother as "my first girlfriend." To save you time, tears, and the cost of that overpriced cocktail you'll nurse while pretending to listen, we've compiled the essential archetypes to avoid.

---

## 1. The Gym Evangelist

He doesn't *have* a personality; he has a protein regimen. Every conversation somehow circles back to his "gains," his macros, or his ongoing feud with a man named Todd from his CrossFit box. He'll photograph his meals not for Instagram, but to send to you unprompted with the caption "fuel 💪." When you suggest pizza, he looks at you like you've proposed a mild crime. Run—but stretch first, he'd want that.

## 2. The Aspiring Podcaster

He has 47 downloads and the confidence of a man with 47 million. He'll explain things you already know, in a voice he's specifically cultivated for "the mic." Warning signs include the phrase "so I was talking about this on the show," and a home decorated exclusively with foam panels and ego.

## 3. The Ex-Obsessed Historian

Crystal did *what* to him in 2019? You'll know. You'll know in exhaustive detail before the appetizers arrive. He's not over her—he's writing a dissertation on her. Every restaurant reminds him of a place they went, and every love song is "kind of their thing." You're not a date; you're a grief counselor with worse pay.

## 4. The Perpetual "Entrepreneur"

His business card says CEO. His CEO position is of a company that exists primarily as a domain name he purchased at 2 a.m. He'll ask you to "invest in his vision" by the second date and describe himself as a "disruptor," though the only thing he's disrupting is your peace.

## 5. The Chronically Unbothered

Texts back in three to five business days. Emotionally available on a "need-to-know basis," and he's decided you don't need to know. Ask him how he feels and he'll say "it's chill." Everything is chill. His entire personality is a shrug wearing a beanie.

## 6. The Foodie Who Can't Cook

He knows the difference between 14 types of olive oil but cannot operate a stove. He'll critique the restaurant's plating while ordering the equivalent of chicken tenders. Prepare for lengthy monologues about "mouthfeel" delivered by a man whose home fridge contains one condiment and existential regret.

## 7. The Man-Child Gamer

His apartment is a shrine to unwashed dishes and unlocked achievements. He'll pause a raid to greet you, which he considers an enormous romantic gesture. His love language is "watching me play," and his life goal is to remain exactly as he is, forever, in this beanbag.

## 8. The Overly Enlightened One

He did ayahuasca once and hasn't stopped talking about it. He'll tell you your aura is "cluttered" and recommend a cleanse. Fiercely spiritual until the check comes, at which point the universe mysteriously fails to provide.

---

## The Bottom Line

If your date checks more than two of these boxes, congratulations—you've unlocked a story for brunch. Grab your friends, order the bottomless mimosas, and remember: the best relationships start with knowing exactly what to avoid.

*Next week: "The Women's Guide to Ghosting With Grace (And a Clear Conscience)."*

# The Nine "Over" Men: A Field Guide to Romantic Regret

Everyone has a type. Maybe yours is tall and mysterious, maybe it's short and funny, maybe it's "employed." Whatever your particular flavor of romantic doom, we've all got that magnetic pull toward certain people—and, more importantly, certain *disasters*.

But before you swipe right on your next questionable decision, allow me to introduce a category of men that transcends height, hairline, and horoscope. I call them the "Over" Men. Because whatever they're doing, they're doing *too much* of it.

Consider this your field guide.

---

**1. The Oversharer**
You've been dating three days and you already know about his childhood bedwetting, his cousin's tax fraud, and his complicated feelings about his ex named Brenda. Talking to him is like reading someone else's diary that you never asked for. He's the human equivalent of a *This American Life* episode that won't end. Boundaries? Never heard of her.

**2. The Overachiever**
He's up at 4 a.m. for cold plunges, runs a side hustle selling artisanal beard oil, and treats brunch like a networking event. You wanted a boyfriend; you got a LinkedIn notification. He's basically Patrick Bateman if *American Psycho* were about optimizing your morning routine instead of, well, you know.

**3. The Overthinker**
This man will spend forty-five minutes analyzing whether the waiter *actually* liked him. Every text you send is decoded like it's the Zodiac Killer's cipher. He's Hamlet, if Hamlet had a Notes app full of things he *almost* said. To be anxious, or not to be anxious—there is no question, it's always anxious.

**4. The Overpromiser**
"We'll go to Italy!" "I'll fix your sink!" "I'm going to start a podcast!" He's got the vision board of a motivational speaker and the follow-through of a New Year's resolution. Trusting his plans is like trusting *Game of Thrones* to stick the landing. Beautiful setup, catastrophic delivery.

**5. The Overgrooming Guy**
His skincare shelf has more products than your entire pharmacy. He's got opinions on jade rollers and takes longer to get ready than you do. Which would be fine—except he'll also comment on *your* pores. He's a modern-day Narcissus, except instead of a pond, he's got a ring light and a front-facing camera.

**6. The Overcompensator**
Loud truck, louder opinions, and a personality built entirely around things he owns. He's aggressively into whatever screams "I have nothing to prove," which is exactly how you know he's got everything to prove. Somewhere, Freud is taking notes and nodding slowly.

**7. The Over-It Guy**
Nothing impresses him. Not the sunset, not the Michelin-starred meal, not your best story. His personality is a shrug in human form. Dating him is like performing to an audience of one guy checking his phone. He's Jughead if Jughead gave up on the crown *and* the mystery.

**8. The Overstayer**
The party ended two hours ago. So did the relationship, emotionally. But he's still *here*, physically and metaphorically, eating your snacks and refusing to read the room. He's the house guest who becomes a roommate who becomes a legal situation. Think Kramer barging in, but you can't laugh it off.

**9. The Overlord**
The controlling one. He needs to know where you are, who you're with, and why you didn't text back in nine minutes. Red flags so bold they could be seen from space. He's giving *Beauty and the Beast*—except the castle never turns back into a mansion and there's no talking teapot to soften the vibe.

---

**The Takeaway**

The trouble with the "Over" Men isn't that they lack qualities—it's that they've got *too many* of the wrong ones, turned up to eleven. A little ambition, a little grooming, a little emotional depth? Wonderful. But moderation, gentlemen, is a virtue.

So the next time you feel that familiar spark, ask yourself one crucial question: *Is he a type... or is he a warning?*

Because everyone has a type. The goal is to make sure yours doesn't come with a subtitle that reads "*based on a true crime story.*"

# The Boyfriend Bestiary: A Field Guide to Men Who Are *Too* Much of a Thing

*In which we catalog the species of romantic disaster you should observe from a safe distance, preferably from behind a locked door.*

Listen, we've all dated someone whose single defining trait eventually revealed itself to be a load-bearing wall in the crumbling architecture of the relationship. The problem isn't that these men have *no* qualities. The problem is that they have exactly one, cranked to eleven, like a smoke alarm you can't reach. Let's meet them.

---

## 1. The Too-Intense One

He doesn't *watch* movies, he *experiences* them. He doesn't *disagree*, he *goes to war*. Everything is a passion, a betrayal, or a hill worth dying on—including the correct way to load a dishwasher.

This is your Russell Crowe boyfriend, and I mean that with love and a healthy sense of self-preservation. On a good day, he's fighting for your honor in a metaphorical Colosseum. On a bad day, he's throwing a metaphorical telephone at a hotel concierge because you suggested you two "maybe stay in tonight." Are you not entertained? You're *exhausted.* You just wanted to talk about brunch and now you're both weeping about the concept of loyalty.

**Warning sign:** He has cried during a sporting event that he was not personally competing in.

---

## 2. The Too-Ambitious One

He has a five-year plan, a ten-year plan, and a contingency plan for when you inevitably become "an obstacle to the vision." You are not a girlfriend; you are a strategic asset with a good couch.

This is your Chuck Bass, minus the billion dollars that makes it aspirational instead of alarming. He'll say something like "I'm not a stop along the way, I'm a destination," and you'll swoon for approximately four seconds before realizing that means *you* are just a stop along the way. He schemes. He broods in a purple scarf. He acquires things—hotels, enemies, occasionally you—and calls it romance.

**Warning sign:** He has referred to your relationship as a "merger" and was not joking.

---

## 3. The Too-Determined One

Ah, the Tracy Flick of boyfriends. He is *going to win.* Win what? Everything. The argument, the group trivia night, the affection of your parents, the imaginary election for Most Committed Partner that only he is running in.

He will lick every envelope. He will make the cupcakes. He will destroy anyone who threatens his campaign for Boyfriend of the Year with a smile so tight it could deflect bullets. The scariest part? He's not even wrong most of the time, which makes it impossible to break up with him without a formal recount. Pick him, choose him, love him—or he *will* find out why you didn't, and he *will* file a complaint.

**Warning sign:** He remembers a slight from the third date and has been quietly compiling evidence ever since.

---

## 4. The Too-Chill One

The reverse boss battle. Nothing bothers him. Nothing moves him. You could announce you're leaving for Mongolia and he'd say "cool, cool, cool" and return to his podcast. At first this feels like serenity. Later you realize you have been dating a beige throw pillow with opinions about cryptocurrency.

**Warning sign:** You cried in front of him once and he offered you a fist bump.

---

## 5. The Too-Nice One

Suspiciously nice. Aggressively agreeable. A man with no edges, no preferences, and a horrifying willingness to eat wherever you want, forever. This one is a trap, because you will spend the entire relationship trying to find out what he actually *thinks*, only to discover the terrifying truth: nothing. There is nothing back there. Just a smile and the phrase "whatever makes you happy."

**Warning sign:** He has never once picked the restaurant, and you're starting to think he might not need to eat at all.

---

## The Takeaway

A good boyfriend, it turns out, is a balanced dish—a little ambition, a little intensity, a little determination, seasoned lightly. The men above forgot the recipe and just poured one ingredient directly into the pan.

So the next time you meet someone charming, ask yourself: is he a whole person, or is he simply *one adjective wearing a nice jacket*?

And if he starts campaigning, licking envelopes, or throwing telephones—

Run. Preferably to a destination he can't strategically acquire.
